english.title: Misuse profits of non commercial prize / equal chance gaming
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) used a part of the profits of

(A)_[non-commercial prize gaming in respect of which a fund-raising purpose had been specified , namely **(..SPECIFY THE SPECIFIED PURPOSE..), as mentioned in section 299(2)]_
(B)_[non-commercial equal-chance gaming in respect of which a fund-raising purpose had been specified, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SPECIFIED PURPOSE..), as mentioned in section 300(2)]_

of the Gambling Act 2005 for another purpose, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OTHER PURPOSE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 301(2) and (4) of the Gambling Act 2005.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 301(3) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that the use of profits includes a reference to permitting profits to be used.
(ii) The meaning of "profits" is provided in sections 299(6) and 300(8) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
